title: Problems involving perimeter and area of composite plane figures
summary: Decompose plane figures, subtract cut-outs and account for shared edges.
objectives: Split a composite figure into familiar plane shapes.
Use subtraction for holes and cut-outs.
Find outside perimeter without counting internal shared edges.

blocks.text: Decompose plane figures, subtract cut-outs and account for shared edges. Keep every measurement in compatible units before substituting.

A composite plane figure can be partitioned into non-overlapping familiar shapes or enclosed in a large shape with cut-outs subtracted. Area counts internal coverage. Perimeter follows only the outside boundary, so shared internal edges are excluded.

Mark every required length before calculating. Missing boundary lengths often come from subtraction along a common total width or height. For area, choose a decomposition that avoids overlap. For perimeter, trace the boundary once in order and list each exposed segment.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 4 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Find the remaining area.

sections.verification_note: The result uses compatible units and agrees with the dimensions and component structure.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: A 14 m by 10 m rectangle has a 6 m by 4 m corner removed. Find both the remaining area and the outside perimeter.

content.text: Removing a corner replaces two outer lengths by two equal inner lengths, so the total perimeter remains 2(14+10).

sections.verification_note: The remaining area is smaller than 140 m², and the boundary trace closes without counting internal edges.

blocks.text: Do not add the area of a cut-out. Do not count shared edges in the outside perimeter. Area and perimeter use different units and cannot be combined in the same arithmetic expression.

prompt.text: A 10 cm by 6 cm rectangle has a 2 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Find the remaining area in cm².

blocks.text: Sketch or decompose the figure, label compatible units, select the correct area or volume relationship, calculate in clear stages, and check that the final unit is squared or cubed as required.
